scope: Round-2 adversarial meta-audit of the second real-entity repair (Merritt -> Tessendale). Every factual assertion in generator_meta.originality_note was independently reproduced from the primary source rather than taken on trust: the GeoNames US dump was re-downloaded and re-counted locally, the Levenshtein screen was re-run (and re-run again over a WIDER name pool than the note used), and every index query in the note (Wikipedia insource, Wikidata wbsearchentities, ROR, OpenAlex institutions, OpenAlex authors, open-web semantic search) was re-issued. Every named entity in the current passage was independently web-verified. The round-1 blocker was re-verified as genuinely remediated.
verification_method_note: The round-1 failure mode being guarded against was agents certifying checks they never ran. Accordingly nothing below is inherited from the note or from the round-1 audit: US.zip was re-fetched from download.geonames.org (HTTP 200, 70,946,132 bytes) into the session scratchpad and all gazetteer claims were recomputed from that file. Wikipedia/Wikidata/ROR/OpenAlex were queried live. Where the note cites a figure, the figure was recomputed, not read.

findings.claim: ROUND-1 BLOCKER IS GENUINELY REMEDIATED. The real Ohio populated place 'Merritt' no longer appears anywhere in the shipped unit; the invented sixteen-week cello trial is now attached to 'Tessendale, Ohio', for which no bearer exists in any index checked.
findings.evidence: Structured field scan of candidates-final/elf-b1-001.json: 'Merritt' occurs 0 times in the passage, 0 times in any prompt/option/key/rationale, and 0 times in generator_meta once originality_note is excluded. The only 5 surviving occurrences are inside originality_note itself, which necessarily narrates the repair and cites the GNIS/GeoNames control case. Current passage carries 'Tessendale' x2 (para 2 setting, para 5 'the Tessendale data'), 'Thelbury' x2, 'Pellerham' x2. The round-1 blocker premise was itself re-verified from primary sources this round and was correct: GeoNames US dump row 4518108|Merritt|Merritt|39.02841|-81.85097|P|PPL|US|OH|105, cross-read against geo.mytopo.com/feature/ohio/meigs/populated-place/1062889/merritt/ which returns GNIS ID 1062889, Feature Class 'Populated Place', County Meigs, Ohio, 39.0284122 / -81.8509678, 'Merritt is a populated place located in Meigs County, Ohio. It appears on the Portland USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle.' The GeoNames coordinates and the GNIS coordinates agree to 5 decimal places, confirming the two records are the same feature.
findings.why: The specific defect this unit was refuted for is gone, and gone by removal rather than by re-labelling. The repair also removed the false '(setting, invented; no such Ohio settlement)' annotation rather than leaving it attached to a different name.

findings.claim: EVERY load-bearing quantitative claim in the originality_note reproduces exactly against a freshly downloaded primary source.
findings.evidence: (a) Note: 'US.zip ... retrieved 2026-08-04, 2,241,386 rows'. Reproduced: wc -l US.txt = 2241386. Exact match. (b) Note: 'contains "Merritt" as geonameid 4518108, feature code PPL, admin1 OH, county FIPS 105 (Meigs), 39.02841 / -81.85097'. Reproduced field-for-field by awk on the dump; every one of the six values matches. (c) Note: 'case-insensitive substring grep over all 2,241,386 rows: 0 hits' for Tessendale. Reproduced: grep -ic 'tessendale' US.txt = 0. This grep covers the alternatenames column too, so it is a stronger test than an exact-name match. (d) Note: 'no real US name within edit distance 2; every real name is >=3 edits away'. Reproduced with an independent Levenshtein implementation over the P/A feature classes: 0 names at distance <=2; nearest real names all at distance 3 (Aspendale, Edendale, Ellendale, Evendale, Helendale, Hessdale, Jerseydale, Reesedale, Rosendale, Rosserdale, Teasdale).
findings.why: This is the half of the note that a lazy agent could most easily fabricate, because it reads as machine output. It is not fabricated. The dump was re-fetched and every figure recomputed.

findings.claim: The note's Levenshtein conclusion survives a STRICTER test than the one the note ran.
findings.evidence: The note screened 'unique names' for feature classes P and A. Re-run over a deliberately wider pool built from the name column PLUS the asciiname column PLUS every comma-separated alternate name for all P/A rows -- 474,870 distinct strings, roughly 3.2x the note's pool -- yields 0 strings within Levenshtein distance 2 of 'tessendale'. Independent open-web semantic search (Exa) for 'Tessendale' as a place name returned only different strings: Tessenderlo (Belgium), Tollendal (Ontario), Teesdale (County Durham; also Teesdale, Victoria), Tesselaarsdal (Western Cape), Passendale (West Flanders). No exact bearer surfaced on any backend.
findings.why: Widening the pool can only make a collision easier to find, never harder, so a null result on the wider pool strictly dominates the note's own claim. The toponym is clean.

findings.claim: INDEPENDENT WEB VERIFICATION OF EVERY NAMED ENTITY IN THE CURRENT PASSAGE, replacements included: no real bearer in a related domain. Each index query asserted by the note was re-issued and each returned what the note says it returned.
findings.evidence: 'Thelbury' / 'Thelbury Institute for Lifespan Research': Wikipedia insource:"Thelbury" -> 'There were no results matching the query', no spelling suggestion; Wikidata wbsearchentities -> "search":[] with success:1; api.ror.org/organizations?query=Thelbury -> number_of_results 0, empty items; api.openalex.org/institutions?search=Thelbury -> meta.count 0, empty results; GeoNames US dump -> 0 case-insensitive hits; Exa semantic search for 'Thelbury Institute' returned only real, unrelated aging-neuroscience bodies (Buck Institute Ellerby Lab, Thuret Lab, Center for Vital Longevity, Kavli Institute) and no page containing the string. 'Everett Pellerham': Wikipedia insource:"Pellerham" -> 'There were no results matching the query'; Wikidata -> "search":[]; api.openalex.org/authors?search=Pellerham -> meta.count 0, empty results; GeoNames US dump -> 0 hits; Exa search for the name as a neuroscientist surfaced no bearer of the surname. 'Tessendale': Wikipedia insource -> no results; see the gazetteer findings above. Byline 'Marguerite Osei' (generator_meta only, absent from the passage): Exa surfaced exactly one near bearer, Marguerite Osei-Wusu, Early Intervention Specialist at Howard County Public Schools -- a different, hyphenated compound name, reproducing the note including the employer. 'Ohio': real US state, kept deliberately per the corpus convention of an invented town inside a real state; no invented finding attaches to the state. Unit title 'Slow Learners': Wikipedia intitle:"Slow Learners" -> 'Result 1 of 1', the 2015 American romantic comedy film directed by Don Argott and Sheena M. Joyce -- exactly the single hit the note discloses; the unit asserts nothing about that film and uses the phrase as a generic headline. Corroborating control: the note's claim that the real Lifespan Research Institute exists and is distinct was verified -- api.ror.org returns 'Lifespan Research Institute', https://ror.org/051jvbj60, Mountain View, United States, matching the note's ROR id character for character.
findings.why: Second mandate discharged. No real bearer in a related domain was found for any name the passage carries, and the note's disclosure about the one real look-alike organisation (Lifespan Research Institute) is accurate rather than concealed.

findings.claim: One arithmetic figure in the note does not reproduce: it states the Levenshtein screen ran over '148,711 unique names' for feature classes P and A; recomputing from the same dump gives 148,052.
findings.evidence: Recount over the identical file (row count 2,241,386 matched exactly, so it is the same dump): distinct values of the name column restricted to feature class P or A = 148,052, a shortfall of 659 against the stated 148,711. The discrepancy is almost certainly a dedup-methodology difference -- pooling the asciiname column or alternate names inflates the pool -- rather than a different corpus.
findings.why: Minor and non-load-bearing: the note's SUBSTANTIVE claim (no real name within edit distance 2) reproduces on the note's own pool and also on a deliberately wider 474,870-name pool, and a larger pool can only surface more collisions, not fewer. Recorded because the audit contract is that every figure in the note must be reproducible, and this one is not exactly reproducible as stated. It should be restated with the dedup rule it actually used.

findings.claim: The round-1 keying inconsistency was NOT fixed and has now been duplicated into the round-2 records: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl uses target 'q1'..'q5' while verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl, verdicts-gstem.jsonl and verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl all use 'q:1'..'q:5'.
findings.evidence: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl elf-b1-001 records at lines 1-5 (entityfix) and 10-14 (entityfix-r2) all carry "target": "qN"; the corresponding verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl records at the same line numbers carry "target": "q:N". Both gates otherwise agree (all 20 G-KEY records pass).
findings.why: Carried forward from the round-1 audit, where it was raised and not acted on. Any consumer joining G-KEY vote-1 to vote-2 on (candidate_id, gate, target) will fail to pair them and could silently read the two-vote G-KEY gate as two independent one-vote gates. Cosmetic today, load-bearing the moment the two votes disagree.

findings.claim: The note's stated scope limits are accurate and were not silently exceeded; the one authority it says it could not reach was independently cross-checked.
findings.evidence: The note discloses that USGS GNIS was not queried directly because its web app is a JavaScript SPA, and that the GNIS-derived GeoNames dump was used instead, cross-read against two GNIS-derived gazetteers on the Merritt control case. That cross-read was reproduced here: geo.mytopo.com returned GNIS ID 1062889 with coordinates agreeing with the GeoNames record to 5 decimals. The note also discloses that no trademark register, no non-US national gazetteer and no paywalled people-search index was queried -- and it does not claim clearance beyond those indexes.
findings.why: A search log that states what it did NOT check is the correct form, and this one states it honestly. The residual exposure (a non-US bearer of 'Tessendale', or a trademark) is real but small: the toponym is asserted to be in Ohio, and the open-web semantic sweep was not geographically restricted and still surfaced no exact bearer.
